text:
IncidentBot: paging: Datadog ingestion delays detected in us-west-2 — increased log/metric tail latencies and missing traces. Severity: P2. Alerts may be arriving late.
PagerDuty: triggered oncall Maya S (primary).
Maya S: seeing gaps on dashboards too — some service graphs flatlined around 22:10 UTC. Not sure if it's metric retention or ingestion lag.
Samir: checking our datadog-agent -> backend metrics now. can everyone avoid mass replays until we know more?
Priya K: confirmed: host-level dd.agent metrics show send_queue_size rising on multiple hosts. Logs show 429s from intake endpoint.
Alex L: I pulled Datadog status: https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents — they list an "Ingestion delay in US region" incident. Matches timing.
Maya S: customer impact: dashboards and alerts may be delayed up to ~10-15m. No evidence of model inference impact, but SLO alerting might not fire.
Samir: rapid mitigation plan: 1) switch critical alerting to CloudWatch fallback for next 30m 2) enable local buffering to S3 for agents with persistent queue growth 3) mute noisy alerts that will spam oncall
Priya K: copy. I'll flip the alert fallback runbook now. Patch to alerting:
```
# route critical alerts to cloudwatch-fallback
for rule in $(cat critical_rules.txt); do
  ./alertctl set-route $rule cloudwatch-fallback
done
```
Alex L: I'm going to open a support ticket & escalate with Datadog via the support pane and link the ingest errors (429, 503). Also posting the intake error snippet: `HTTP 429 https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input - rate_limited`
ops-bot: uploaded recent agent logs to /artifacts/2265881234/agent-logs.tar.gz
Maya S: Samir, can you do a quick customer impact assessment? Which customers are on Dedicated vs hosted? Any enterprise customers likely to notice?
Samir: quick list: cust-omega (dedicated west) -> internal telemetry still coming, but hosted clients using Datadog for observability (cust-alpha, cust-beta) will see gaps. Recommending we message cust-alpha support channel: "Observability delays for dataplane events; metrics may be delayed ~10-20m."
Priya K: I've muted health-check alerts on non-critical services to reduce noise. Leaving prod-critical alone but routed to cloudwatch-fallback.
Maya S: handoff note: I'm going to triage for another 15m then hand to Samir for monitoring/cleanup. Leave incident channel open.
Samir: taking over at 22:25 UTC. Action items assigned: Priya (alert routing + buffering), Alex (Datadog escalation + status updates), Maya (customer comms + postmortem note).
Alex L: Datadog responded: "We're experiencing ingestion delays due to upstream throttling, mitigation in progress. Estimated recovery 30-45 minutes." I'll paste updates here.
Maya S: posting customer-facing blurb to support: "We're seeing a 10-30m delay in metrics/log ingestion due to a Datadog regional issue. No impact to inference or core APIs. We'll update when Datadog reports recovery."
Samir: also enabling a temporary local export for critical logs to our S3 bucket so customers can access recent logs if needed. Command I used:
```
# enable s3-forwarder on subset of hosts
kubectl -n infra set env ds/fluentd S3_FORWARD=true
```
Priya K: queue sizes stabilizing on some hosts after throttling config tweak. Still seeing elevated latencies but no continual growth.
IncidentBot: update: Datadog status page now shows partial recovery in US region.
Alex L: Datadog confirms ingestion backlog is draining; they recommend waiting 1 hour for full reconciliation.
Maya S: last checks at 22:32 UTC show dashboards repopulating. Keeping channel open for one hour to ensure no regression.
Samir: leaving a short handoff message for next oncall: monitor alerts that were muted (we'll unmute once Datadog fully healthy), validate any missed alerts against CloudWatch fallback, and include any customer escalations in the postmortem.
Maya S: thanks all. I'll draft the incident timeline and a short RCA focusing on dependency on Datadog ingestion SLAs and suggested mitigations (automatic fallback routing + export buffer).
Priya K: noted. saving artifacts: /artifacts/2265881234/ (logs, tickets, commands used).
ops-bot: closing temporary chat thread markers.
Maya S: incident closed for active mitigation; still monitoring until backlog clear.
